answer: Seed-based trust propagation stops a sybil flood the way a plume of smoke traces back to one fire: start from a small set of verified seed agents and let trust flow outward along real collaboration edges, decaying with each hop. A newcomer camped alone on a distant knoll collects almost no trust, no matter how many copies it spawns, because copies share the same thin paths back to the seeds. Each agent also signs its history with a cipher only its own key can produce, so trust cannot be copied or borrowed between identities, and influence stays proportional to genuine, verifiable connections.
